Peek · Universal Parcel Tracker

Terms of use

Effective 17 November 2026

Peek follows parcels, on the web at peektracker.com and in its iPhone and Android apps. These terms apply when you use the official service, directly or through an assistant you connect to it. The privacy notice says what Peek keeps and why.

Who runs Peek

Peek is a personal, non-commercial project run by Paul-Louis Hery, in Switzerland. It is free: no fees, no subscription and no advertising. Its code is open source under the GNU Affero General Public License 3.0, on GitHub.

Using Peek

  • Peek is for anyone aged 13 or over.
  • Follow parcels you send or expect, or that someone shared with you.
  • Don't try to get around Peek's limits, look up numbers in bulk, break its security or reach other people's data.
  • Peek may limit, suspend or close an account or a connection that breaks these terms or puts the service at risk.

Your account and what you add

  • Your account is tied to your email address, or to your Google or Apple sign-in. Keep access to it: whoever can sign in with it can use the account.
  • What you add stays yours. You let Peek store it and send tracking numbers to carriers and tracking services, as far as that is needed to follow your parcels.
  • Settings › Account & data › Download my data gives you a copy, and Delete account erases the account with its parcels.

What carriers publish

Peek shows what carriers and tracking services publish about a parcel. It is not a carrier, and it cannot redirect, hold or find a parcel. An update can be late, missing or wrong: for anything that matters, check with the carrier or the seller. Carriers' names belong to their owners, and Peek is not affiliated with them.

Assistants and personal tokens

  • An assistant you connect, such as Claude or ChatGPT, acts on your account within what you allowed: it sees your parcels and, if you allowed it, adds and archives them. What it does with that access is between you and its provider, whose own terms apply.
  • You can disconnect an assistant at any time in Settings › Assistants.
  • Peek is not made or endorsed by the companies behind these assistants.

Availability and changes

Peek comes as it is, without guarantees. It may be unavailable at times, and its features may change or end; beta ones in particular. If the service is going to close, Peek says so beforehand where it can, so you have time to download your data.

Liability

As far as the law allows, Peek and the person who runs it are not liable for indirect loss, or for loss caused by an update that was late, missing or wrong, such as a missed delivery. Nothing in these terms limits liability that the law does not allow to be limited, such as for intent or gross negligence.

Changes to these terms

A new version is published on this page with the day it takes effect. Using Peek after that day means you accept it. If you don't, stop using Peek and delete your account.

Law and disputes

Swiss law applies, and the courts of the canton where Peek's operator lives hear disputes. If you use Peek as a consumer, the law of the country you live in may give you protections or courts that these terms cannot take away.

Contact

Write to hello at peektracker.com. For a security concern, use GitHub's private vulnerability report.

These terms cover the official Peek service. A fork is run by someone else, who sets their own terms.
